provenance.notes: Clean family batch, book archetype. Safety-driven, coupon-scarred trade, so copy leans on upfront scope and camera proof, never on health or fire claims. No equipment brands. Fresh Fern fails CTA contrast. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Clothes needing two cycles, a hot laundry room, lint at the outside flap, a burning smell, a bird nest in the vent hood, and what to do before the visit
pageStructurePlus.why: Most dryer vent bookings start with a symptom, not a search for a service. A page that names the symptom is the one they book from.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Supply and return runs, registers, trunk lines, the blower compartment, what counts as one system, and what is quoted separately like coil cleaning
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers have seen cheap whole-house coupons that turn into a bigger bill. A written scope is how an honest duct cleaner wins that buyer.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Before-and-after camera footage of the ducts and the dryer vent run, sent to the homeowner the same day, with notes on anything that needs repair
pageStructurePlus.why: People can't see inside their ducts. Footage they can watch on their phone is the proof that the work was done.

pageStructurePlus.section: Why the duct price doesn't change at the door
pageStructurePlus.contains: Per-vent and per-system pricing explained, what can raise a price and how it's approved first, and a plain note about bait coupons
pageStructurePlus.why: Coupon pricing has made people suspicious of this trade. Saying exactly how the price is set removes the main reason they hesitate.

pageStructurePlus.section: Long runs, roof terminations and rerouting
pageStructurePlus.contains: Dryer vents that exit through the roof or run long in townhomes and condos, rigid duct replacement, bird guards, and how roof access is handled
pageStructurePlus.why: Upper-floor laundry and roof vents are the hard jobs other companies skip. Showing them wins condo owners and property managers.

openers.line: Your Google listing has good dryer vent reviews and no Website button, so someone whose towels need two cycles to dry has nowhere to see what you charge.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where a dryer vent search could land instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook, and the duct cleaning price there is in a post from last year. People who have been burned by coupons want the current price in writing.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and note where it lands and the date of the newest price post.
openers.linkLine: Your duct cleaning price, current and in writing: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page with a broken contact form and no list of what a duct cleaning includes. A careful homeowner reads that as the coupon crowd.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one broken or missing thing: a dead form, no scope, an old number. Note it.
openers.linkLine: A duct cleaning page with the scope written out: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your vent cleaning site wouldn't load past the header on my phone. People look this up standing next to a hot dryer, phone in hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Vent cleaning, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no price anywhere for a dryer vent cleaning or a whole-system duct cleaning. Buyers who have seen bait coupons trust the company that prints its real number.
openers.hook: Check the listing, posts and any site for a published price. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Upfront dryer vent and duct prices: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-after camera clips from inside the ducts are the best proof this trade has, and they vanish from the feed in a few days.
openers.hook: Find one camera or before-and-after clip on their pages. Mention the house or the run if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your duct camera footage on a page that stays: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say the dryer works like new after your visit. That's the sentence a person with damp towels is searching for, and it should sit next to your dryer vent price.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about drying time or lint. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your dryer vent reviews beside the Book button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The first cold week, people switch the furnace on, smell the dust and search for air duct cleaning. The company with a booking page that week gets the calendar.
openers.hook: Use in September and October, before heating season. Check for a seasonal post.
openers.linkLine: Air duct cleaning booked before the furnace kicks on: {demo-link}

openers.line: When a home inspector flags a dryer vent during a sale, the seller has a few days to fix it. A dryer vent page with a quick booking catches those deadlines.
openers.hook: Use if they mention realtors, inspections or closings in posts or reviews.
openers.linkLine: Dryer vent fixes for inspection deadlines: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a duct cleaning technician. Applicants check whether the company looks solid before they climb into somebody's attic for you.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign on the van. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A duct cleaning page with a hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews come from {Neighborhood} and towns around it, but nothing online lists where your vent cleaning van goes, so people at the edge assume it's too far.
openers.hook: Find the furthest town named in their reviews or posts and use it.
openers.linkLine: A coverage page for your vent cleaning van: {demo-link}

openers.line: Upper-floor condos with dryer vents through the roof are the jobs most vent cleaners skip. If you do them, a page saying so wins every condo board in town.
openers.hook: Look for a roof, condo or townhome job in their posts. Only use this if they do roof access.
openers.linkLine: Roof and condo dryer vents on one page: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Insured in the attic and on the roof
openers.line: Letting a crew into the attic and onto the roof for a vent cleaning is a trust call. If you're insured, that belongs on the page right next to the price.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' on their listing, van or posts. Never claim what you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and scope on one vent cleaning page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like a lot of your duct cleaning comes from HVAC companies passing jobs on. That's great until one of them buys their own duct equipment.
openers.hook: Look for posts or reviews that mention an HVAC company or a furnace tech. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where referred duct cleaning customers should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is exactly what a worried homeowner wants to see from a vent cleaner. It belongs on a page they can book from.
openers.hook: Pick their newest duct or dryer vent post and name it: the lint pile, the bird nest, the long run.
openers.linkLine: That vent cleaning job on a page that books: {demo-link}

objections.objection: I don't want to post prices, the coupon guys undercut me.
objections.handler: "You're not competing with the coupon. You're the company that says what the full duct cleaning costs and what's included. The careful buyers are looking for exactly that."

objections.objection: My work comes from HVAC companies.
objections.handler: "Keep those. The site is for the homeowner the HVAC tech mentioned you to, who looks you up before calling, and for the day one of those companies starts doing duct cleaning themselves."

objections.objection: Dryer vents are too cheap to bother marketing.
objections.handler: "The dryer vent is the door. That same house needs the ducts done, a bird guard, maybe a reroute, and a reminder every year. The site sells all of it."

objections.objection: I'm too busy in the fall.
objections.handler: "That's why I built it first. I need about twenty minutes and your price list. Your busy season is when an online booking page saves you the most calls."

objections.objection: I tried a website before and got nothing.
objections.handler: "Was there a price on it, and a list of what the duct cleaning includes? That's what's different here. People in this trade buy from whoever looks honest first."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's upfront prices, the scope page, the warning-signs page and booking. A handful of whole-system duct jobs covers it."

bullets: Peg the build to a handful of whole-system duct jobs, never to the dryer vent price.
The upfront price page and the written scope are the core. Everything else is added around them.
Price the camera report feature by how the footage gets to the homeowner: a link per job costs more to set up than a gallery.
Charge separately for condo and multi-unit pages; property managers are a different buyer with a different form.
Keep monthly items small next to one dryer vent visit, so the owner never weighs them against a job.
Never write health or fire-risk claims into the copy you sell; price the warning-signs page as plain symptoms and steps.

withoutAI.route: Home inspectors who flag dryer vents

withoutAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors are one-person shops who need a site and already trust the vent cleaner they recommend.

withoutAI.whoPays: The appliance repair shop, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The appliance tech who tells customers their dryer vent is clogged and sends them to you needs a booking page for repairs."

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The condo manager who books your building-wide dryer vent day still sends notices on paper. A resident page fixes that."

withoutAI.route: Realtors who need fast inspection fixes
